claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch now despite an unresolved evaluation gap in a named regulated-customer segment, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and governance through documentation and post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the release policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Low-volume or non-core product labels do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
If the limitation is material, policy requires it to be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public governance guidance can support documentation and monitoring practices, but it cannot override the internal release-policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the health-plan benefits support gap must be disclosed.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering the named segment limitation before launch.
Executed or draft model-card/customer disclosure text showing the limitation has been disclosed for the named use case.
Evidence clarifying whether the regulated-customer pilot use case is a named launch use case under the release process.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support general launch readiness but do not resolve the separate disclosure predicate for a material limitation.
The affected segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, which weighs toward materiality under the provided policy text.
Product's 'non-core' characterization is not sufficient to negate materiality when the segment is tied to customer commitments.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so the record does not show the issue is resolved or approved for risk acceptance before launch.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch; no admissible evidence shows either condition is satisfied.
unsupported_claims: That current evidence is sufficient to justify immediate certification as compliant.
That model-card guidance and ongoing monitoring can substitute for resolving or formally accepting a policy-triggering disclosure issue before launch.
Any implication that the named segment gap is immaterial on the current admissible record.
